Sean / team —

Attached is a working draft and an evidence matrix (evidence-matrix.xlsx) showing what infra/CS can reasonably produce. High-level position and three options below.

Option A (preferred, mutual exclusion):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, special, incidental, indirect or punitive damages, including lost profits, loss of business, or loss of data, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability or otherwise, except to the extent such damages arise from (i) a party's willful misconduct or gross negligence, or (ii) a party's breach of its obligations under Section X (IP indemnities)."

Rationale: Keeps symmetry (sales-friendly) and limits carveouts to higher culpability or IP; preserves commercial predictability.

Option B (one-way Atlas-favored, with evidentiary gate):
"Atlas shall not be liable for consequential, special, incidental, indirect or punitive damages. Redwood may seek such damages only if Atlas satisfies the evidentiary requirements described below and demonstrates by preponderance of the evidence that: (i) Atlas's act or omission was the proximate cause of the alleged loss; (ii) the loss is quantifiable and documented in accordance with the Evidence Requirements; and (iii) Redwood provided Atlas with written notice and a 30-day opportunity to remediate. Evidence Requirements: post-incident report, contemporaneous telemetry and logs, customer billing statements showing loss, and an independent technical report if causation is disputed."

Rationale: Preserves Atlas's request but raises the proof bar. Biggest operational risk: independent report requirement may be expensive and slow.

Option C (compromise with capped residual exposure):
Mutual exclusion but allow recovery for excluded damages only up to a capped amount (e.g., greater of $250,000 or 3x fees in prior 12 months) where the Evidence Requirements are met; include early-notice/remediation step.

Practical evidence matrix (what infra/CS can produce):
- Request/transaction logs (up to 90 days retention per default)
- System metrics and traces (sampled)
- Request IDs and payload headers (where available)
- Post-incident RCA prepared by our SREs (can be provided within 30–60 days for major incidents)
- Billing ledger entries and timestamps

Ask for sales: if we commit to an independent report as a contractual precondition, require Atlas to pay for it or for costs to be allocated in the SOW.

I'm attaching a marked-up clause (OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf) with inline comments and a short risk note for Sean. If we go with Option B/C, I recommend adding a short onboarding-run checklist in the SOW that documents telemetry retention and log access to set expectations.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form: exclusion language + evidentiary gate

Thanks for the draft, Laura. Atlas appreciates the engagement, but a few points of pushback from counsel's perspective:

1) One-way vs mutual: Atlas will only accept a mutual exclusion if Redwood agrees to more robust service credits and a liquidated-damages style cap on direct damages. Otherwise Atlas insists on the one-way carveout as written in our v3.
2) Evidentiary standard: requiring an "independent technical report" as a precondition to pursue excluded damages is disproportionate; Atlas requests that the evidentiary gate be limited to (i) timely incident notice, (ii) post-incident RCA signed by the accountable product owner, and (iii) billing/financial proof of loss.

Suggested compromise language (for negotiation):
"Claims for consequential, special, incidental or punitive damages are excluded, provided that such exclusion shall not apply where (a) the claiming party has provided written notice within thirty (30) days of the event, (b) the claiming party furnishes a post-incident report signed by the product owner, and (c) the claiming party produces contemporaneous logs and billing records reasonably sufficient to quantify the claimed loss. In the event causation is disputed, the parties shall jointly select a neutral technical expert to prepare a binding report; costs shall be apportioned equally unless the expert finds in favor of one party on the threshold issue of causation."

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept this narrower independent-expert trigger (i.e., expert only if causation is disputed) and whether Redwood will agree to a modest direct-damage cap increase in exchange for a mutual exclusion.

Regards,
Marta Bryan
Bryan Legal for Atlas Data Systems
marta@bryanlegal.com
